candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The pipe friction factor f_D is a dimensionless quantity characterizing frictional losses in pipe flow, commonly defined as a function of Reynolds number and relative roughness, both dimensionless. Given the input variables (fluid density rho, dynamic viscosity mu, pipe diameter D, mean flow velocity U, and absolute wall roughness epsilon), the friction factor f_D is dimensionless, as it represents a ratio of forces or pressure losses normalized by dynamic pressure and pipe geometry, hence it has no physical dimension.
